## `SmokeCheck`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.SmokeCheck` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One registered smoke check: an id, the phase that owns it, and the work to run. Pure logic - the check body is supplied by whoever registers it, so this type stays free of Unity and BepInEx and can be unit-tested off-engine.

<a id="smokecheck--ctor-string-string-func-smokecheckresult"></a>

### `SmokeCheck(string id, string phase, Func<SmokeCheckResult> run)`

Creates a check.

**Parameters**

- `id`: Stable id, e.g. `p0.paths`. Required; also the report key.
- `phase`: Phase label of the check, e.g. `P0`. Required.
- `run`: The check body. Must not be null; it may throw (see [`SmokeCheck.Execute`](#smokecheck--execute)).

<a id="smokecheck--ctor-string-string-func-smokecheckresult-bool"></a>

### `SmokeCheck(string id, string phase, Func<SmokeCheckResult> run, bool loud)`

Creates a check, saying whether running it is something the player notices.

**Parameters**

- `id`: Stable id, e.g. `p0.paths`. Required; also the report key.
- `phase`: Phase label of the check, e.g. `P0`. Required.
- `run`: The check body. Must not be null; it may throw (see [`SmokeCheck.Execute`](#smokecheck--execute)).
- `loud`: True when running the check is something the player sees or hears (see [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud)).

<a id="smokecheck--ctor-string-string-func-smokecheckresult-bool-action"></a>

### `SmokeCheck(string id, string phase, Func<SmokeCheckResult> run, bool loud, Action restore)`

Creates a check that puts back whatever running it changed.

**Parameters**

- `id`: Stable id, e.g. `p0.paths`. Required; also the report key.
- `phase`: Phase label of the check, e.g. `P0`. Required.
- `run`: The check body. Must not be null; it may throw (see [`SmokeCheck.Execute`](#smokecheck--execute)).
- `loud`: True when running the check is something the player sees or hears (see [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud)).
- `restore`: Optional undo, run after the body whatever the body did (see [`SmokeCheck.Restore`](#smokecheck--restore)).

<a id="smokecheck--id"></a>

### `string Id { get; }`

Stable id; the key this check is reported under.

<a id="smokecheck--loud"></a>

### `bool Loud { get; }`

True when the check is something the player notices: it plays a clip, repaints the character, opens a window. Only a [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](#smokerunmode--loud) run includes these (see [`SmokeTriggers.Includes`](#smoketriggers--includes)); the hotkey, the trigger file and an automatic run all report them as skipped, so nothing the player can see happens unless someone asked for it by name (`smoke run loud`).

<a id="smokecheck--phase"></a>

### `string Phase { get; }`

Phase label of this check (`P0`, `P1`, ...).

<a id="smokecheck--restore"></a>

### `Action Restore { get; }`

What puts the game back the way it was before [`SmokeCheck.Run`](#smokecheck--run) touched it, or null when the check changes nothing lasting.

A loud check used to read the old facial/motion/look value only to describe the delta and never wrote it back, so one smoke run left Satone smiling at a motion nobody chose. A check that changes visible state declares the undo here and [`SmokeCheck.ExecuteAndRestore`](#smokecheck--executeandrestore) runs it in a `finally` - so it runs even when the body throws, and a failing undo is reported rather than aborting the run.

<a id="smokecheck--run"></a>

### `Func<SmokeCheckResult> Run { get; }`

The check body. Prefer [`SmokeCheck.Execute`](#smokecheck--execute), which times it and cannot throw.

<a id="smokecheck--asloud"></a>

### `SmokeCheck AsLoud()`

This check marked [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud); returns the same instance if it already is.

<a id="smokecheck--execute"></a>

### `SmokeCheckResult Execute()`

Runs the check, times it, and reports it under [`SmokeCheck.Id`](#smokecheck--id). Never throws: a check that fails, throws, or returns nothing all become a failed result. The exception is not swallowed - its type and message become [`SmokeCheckResult.Detail`](#smokecheckresult--detail), which the runner logs as an error line and writes into the report.

<a id="smokecheck--executeandrestore"></a>

### `SmokeCheckResult ExecuteAndRestore(Action<SmokeCheck, Exception> onRestoreFailed)`

Runs the check and then its [`SmokeCheck.Restore`](#smokecheck--restore), in a `finally`: the undo happens whatever the body did, and an undo that itself fails is handed to `onRestoreFailed` instead of escaping. Never throws, except for a null `onRestoreFailed`, which is a programming error caught before anything runs.

**Parameters**

- `onRestoreFailed`: Called with this check and the exception when [`SmokeCheck.Restore`](#smokecheck--restore) throws. Required: the framework does not log from this assembly, so the caller is where a failed undo becomes a visible line. Not called when there is no [`SmokeCheck.Restore`](#smokecheck--restore), and it must not throw.

**Returns:** The same result [`SmokeCheck.Execute`](#smokecheck--execute) would return.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `onRestoreFailed` is null.

<a id="smokecheck--withrestore"></a>

### `SmokeCheck WithRestore(Action restore)`

This check with `restore` as its undo; returns the same instance when it already has that undo.

**Parameters**

- `restore`: The undo to attach, or null to drop the one it has.

<a id="smokecheckresult--ctor-string-bool-string-long-bool"></a>

Creates a result, saying whether a failure is only "not exercised yet".

**Parameters**

- `ok`: Whether the check passed.
- `detail`: Human-readable evidence; `null` becomes an empty string.

- `informational`: True when a false `ok` means "nothing has exercised this yet" rather than "this is broken" (see [`SmokeCheckResult.Informational`](#smokecheckresult--informational)).

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: `elapsedMs` is negative.

<a id="smokecheckresult--detail"></a>

<a id="smokecheckresult--elapsedms"></a>

<a id="smokecheckresult--informational"></a>

### `bool Informational { get; }`

True when a failure is only "the game has not done this yet this session".

Half the early checks report what has been *observed* - Satone changing state, a pomodoro running, a line with text. Three seconds into a launch none of them can have happened, and the runner logging them at Error painted a healthy session red. The verdict is still not ok, because the check has not proved anything; the level it is announced at is Warning.

A check that has not been exercised yet: not ok, but [`SmokeCheckResult.Informational`](#smokecheckresult--informational), so it is announced at Warning rather than Error. Use it for every "not yet observed" / "not exercised" verdict, and keep [`SmokeCheckResult.Fail`](#smokecheckresult--fail) for a seam that is actually broken.

<a id="smokepassschedule"></a>

## `SmokePassSchedule`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.SmokePassSchedule` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

When the automatic second smoke pass runs, expressed as pure arithmetic so it can be unit-tested without an engine.

A single pass a few seconds after the scene loads cannot see anything the game has not done yet: checks that report "observed at least once this session" (`p1.events.satone_state` is the usual one) are red simply because the player has been in the room for three seconds. Running the whole set again a minute in fixes that — at the price of a second unannounced run, which is why it is off by default. Set `Smoke.SecondPassSeconds` to [`SmokePassSchedule.SuggestedSecondPassSeconds`](#smokepassschedule--suggestedsecondpassseconds) to get it back.

<a id="smokepassschedule--defaultsecondpassseconds"></a>

### `const float DefaultSecondPassSeconds = 0.0f`

Default of `Smoke.SecondPassSeconds`: off. The framework no longer runs itself unasked, because each pass plays the test clip and repaints the character.

<a id="smokepassschedule--minimumgapseconds"></a>

### `const float MinimumGapSeconds = 0.5f`

Shortest gap the framework will leave between the two passes. A second pass in the same frame as the first would re-read the same counters and prove nothing, so a configured value at or below the settle delay is pushed out to here instead of being refused.

<a id="smokepassschedule--suggestedsecondpassseconds"></a>

### `const float SuggestedSecondPassSeconds = 60.0f`

The value that made a hands-off launch end green: one minute after the scene loads, late enough for the "observed this session" checks to have seen something. Not a default any more, but the number to put in the config when you want that behaviour.

<a id="smokepassschedule--isenabled"></a>

### `static bool IsEnabled(float secondPassSeconds)`

True when `secondPassSeconds` asks for a second pass at all.

**Parameters**

- `secondPassSeconds`: The configured `Smoke.SecondPassSeconds`.

**Returns:** False for 0, for a negative value, and for NaN/infinity - all of which mean "off".

<a id="smokepassschedule--tryplansecondpass"></a>

### `static bool TryPlanSecondPass(float settleSeconds, float secondPassSeconds, out float delayAfterFirstPass)`

How long the runner waits after the first pass has finished before running the second.

**Parameters**

- `settleSeconds`: Delay between the scene load and the first pass.
- `secondPassSeconds`: Delay between the scene load and the second pass.
- `delayAfterFirstPass`: Seconds to wait once the first pass is done; meaningful only when this returns true.

**Returns:** True when a second pass is wanted.

## `SmokeRegistry`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.SmokeRegistry` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Process-wide list of smoke checks. Static because the plugins that contribute checks are separate BepInEx assemblies with no reference to each other: each one registers on Awake and the single runner in CwyLs.ModLoader executes whatever it finds. Every member takes the same lock, so registration from a plugin thread while the runner snapshots on the main thread is safe.

<a id="smokeregistry--count"></a>

### `static int Count { get; }`

Number of registered checks.

<a id="smokeregistry--clear"></a>

### `static void Clear()`

Removes every registered check. Used by tests; harmless at runtime.

<a id="smokeregistry--register-smokecheck"></a>

### `static void Register(SmokeCheck check)`

Registers a check. Re-registering an existing [`SmokeCheck.Id`](#smokecheck--id) replaces it in place (keeping its position), so a plugin that runs Awake twice cannot double-report.

<a id="smokeregistry--register-smokecheck-bool"></a>

### `static void Register(SmokeCheck check, bool loud)`

Registers a check, marking it [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud) when it is something the player sees or hears. A loud check runs only on an explicit trigger (the hotkey or the trigger file); an automatic run reports it as skipped instead of playing a clip or repainting the character behind the player's back.

**Parameters**

- `check`: The check. Required.
- `loud`: True to mark it loud. False leaves [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud) as the check was built with, so a check constructed loud stays loud through the plain overload.

<a id="smokeregistry--register-smokecheck-bool-action"></a>

### `static void Register(SmokeCheck check, bool loud, Action restore)`

Registers a check together with what puts the game back afterwards. A loud check that changes what the player sees - a facial index, a motion, the look target - must hand in the undo here, and the runner runs it in a `finally` after the body ([`SmokeCheck.ExecuteAndRestore`](#smokecheck--executeandrestore)).

**Parameters**

- `check`: The check. Required.
- `loud`: True to mark it loud. False leaves [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud) as the check was built with, so a check constructed loud stays loud through the plain overload.
- `restore`: The undo. Null leaves the check's own [`SmokeCheck.Restore`](#smokecheck--restore) alone, so a check constructed with one keeps it.

<a id="smokeregistry--snapshot"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<SmokeCheck> Snapshot(string phase = null)`

A copy of the registered checks, in registration order. The copy is detached: later registrations never mutate a snapshot a run is already iterating.

**Parameters**

- `phase`: When given, keeps only checks of that [`SmokeCheck.Phase`](#smokecheck--phase) (case-insensitive).

<a id="smokereportwriter--tojson"></a>

The report as one line of JSON: `{"session","ticket","unity","game","time","ok","passed","total","detail","checks":[{"id","ok","informational","detail","elapsedMs"}]}`.

<a id="smokerunmode"></a>

## `SmokeRunMode`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.SmokeRunMode` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Why a smoke run is happening, which decides whether the loud checks take part.

The run mode splits "someone asked" into [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](#smokerunmode--quiet) and [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](#smokerunmode--loud). Asking for a run is not the same as asking the game to play a clip, repaint the character and leave her smiling at a motion nobody chose: the hotkey and the trigger file now produce a quiet run, and only the console command `smoke run loud` or the `smoke.loud` trigger file produce a loud one.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="smokerunmode--automatic"></a>`Automatic` | 0 | Nobody asked: the scene loaded, or the second pass came round. A run like this must be invisible and inaudible, so [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud) checks are skipped. |
| <a id="smokerunmode--explicit"></a>`Explicit` | 1 | The old spelling of [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](#smokerunmode--loud): "someone asked, so run everything". Kept so code written against the old enum keeps compiling and keeps its old meaning; new code should say [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](#smokerunmode--quiet) or [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](#smokerunmode--loud), which say what the player will notice rather than who asked. |
| <a id="smokerunmode--quiet"></a>`Quiet` | 2 | Someone asked, but only for the checks the player cannot notice: the `smoke.run` hotkey and the `BepInEx/smoke.run` trigger file. [`SmokeCheck.Loud`](#smokecheck--loud) checks are reported as skipped ([`SmokeTriggers.QuietSkipDetail`](#smoketriggers--quietskipdetail)). |
| <a id="smokerunmode--loud"></a>`Loud` | 3 | Someone asked for the whole suite, knowing it plays a clip and moves the character: the console command `smoke run loud` or the `BepInEx/smoke.loud` trigger file. Every loud check runs, and every loud check restores what it touched ([`SmokeCheck.Restore`](#smokecheck--restore)). |

<a id="smoketriggers"></a>

## `SmokeTriggers`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Smoke.SmokeTriggers` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What may start a smoke run, and what a run does with the loud checks. Pure constants and three decisions, so all of them can be tested off-engine.

The framework moved from "run itself twice every launch" to "run when asked". The old behaviour played the test beep and stripped and re-applied Satone's textures three seconds into every session and again a minute later, which reads as the game doing something random. Automatic runs are off by default; the hotkey and the trigger file are the two ways to ask for one.

The run mode finished the job: asking for a run is no longer the same as asking for a show. The hotkey and `smoke.run` produce a [`SmokeRunMode.Quiet`](#smokerunmode--quiet) run; the console command `smoke run loud` and the [`SmokeTriggers.LoudTriggerFileName`](#smoketriggers--loudtriggerfilename) file are the only two [`SmokeRunMode.Loud`](#smokerunmode--loud) paths.

Trigger label written by a run asked for in the in-game console.
